title: Study evaluating whether linzagolix or bilastine can reduce breast density in women who have not yet gone through menopause and are at high risk of breast cancer.
official: Breast density reduction with linzagolix or bilastine in premenopausal women at high risk of breast cancer: a phase II clinical trial.
summary: Main objective: To compare the relative change in mammographic breast density from baseline to 12 months between the three study groups (linzagolix, bilastine and control group).

interventions.name: Bilastina Teva 20 mg comprimidos bucodispersables EFG

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Women aged 35 to 50 years.
2. Premenopausal status, defined by the presence of regular menstrual cycles during the previous year or by hormone levels (estradiol and FSH) consistent with normal ovarian function.
3. Estimated 5-year breast cancer risk ≥1.67%, calculated using the Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Tool (Gail model).
4. High mammographic breast density on the baseline mammogram, classified as BI-RADS category C or D.
5. Ability to understand the study information and provide written informed consent.
6. Willingness and ability to comply with all study visits and procedures throughout the study follow-up period.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Personal history of breast cancer or other hormone-dependent cancers.
2. Concomitant treatment with medicinal products contraindicated according to the current Summary of Product Characteristics of linzagolix or bilastine, or with medicinal products presenting clinically relevant interactions that cannot be discontinued or substituted before randomisation.
3. Previous diagnosis of osteoporosis or T-score ≤ −2.5 on bone densitometry performed during the screening process or on available previous examinations.
4. Genital bleeding of unexplained aetiology at the time of inclusion.
5. Clinically relevant impairment of liver function at baseline laboratory testing, defined as AST or ALT >2 times the upper limit of normal, total bilirubin >1.5 times the upper limit of normal, or any other hepatic abnormality that, in the investigator’s judgement, contraindicates participation in the study.
6. Clinically relevant impairment of renal function at baseline laboratory testing, defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m², or any other renal abnormality that, in the investigator’s judgement, contraindicates participation in the study.
7. Personal history of congenital or clinically significant acquired long QT syndrome, clinically relevant arrhythmias, or clinically relevant QT interval prolongation on the baseline ECG.
8. Simultaneous participation in another clinical trial involving medicinal products.
9. Family history of congenital long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden cardiac death in a first-degree relative.
10. Clinically significant bradycardia.
11. Clinically significant hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia or hypocalcaemia not corrected at the time of inclusion.
12. Concomitant treatment with medicinal products known to prolong the QT interval when discontinuation or substitution is not possible.
13. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy or oocyte donation during the study period.
14. Presence of relevant medical conditions or psychiatric disorders that, in the investigator’s judgement, may interfere with participant safety, study adherence, or interpretation of the results.
15. Systemic hormonal treatment within the 12 months prior to inclusion, including hormonal contraceptives, hormone replacement therapy, hormonal treatments for gynaecological conditions, and any other hormonal treatment regardless of its indication or route of administration.
16. Known contraindications to the use of linzagolix or bilastine, including hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of their excipients.
